verdict_vs_market.quote: The offer is market-competitive, not a compelling “leave a job you like” offer.

verdict_vs_current.quote: Without refreshers, Google is only $104,000 better over four years, or about $26,000 per year—a 5% premium.

recommendation.quote: Negotiate. Don’t accept the offer as-is, but don’t reject it yet.

equity_grounding.quote: Recent compensation data puts the 90th percentile for US Google L6 PM compensation near $671,000, so the requested recurring package is high but not outside reported L6 outcomes.

uses_public_incumbent_benchmark.quote: That is almost exactly the current Bay Area median reported for Google L6 PMs—about $551,000

refresh_valued_at.quote: almost all of that attractive upside comes from something the recruiter explicitly said is not guaranteed.

uses_given_refresh_numbers.quote: Under the recruiter’s refresher illustration, Google becomes substantially better: about $480,000 more over four years.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: If they do not improve it: Given that you are happy at Meta and compensation is important, I would probably stay.

unsupported_claims.claim: Google new-hire grants generally vest 38%/32%/20%/10% while refreshes vest evenly over four years.
unsupported_claims.quote: Current public reporting says Google new-hire grants generally vest 38%/32%/20%/10%, while refresh grants generally vest evenly over four years.

missing_info_requested: exact percentage of new-hire grant vesting per year

year1_vs_recurring.quote: Equity raises your recurring four-year package; sign-on protects the transition and compensates for forfeited Meta vesting.
